result.reason: B is clearer: it leads with performance, defines "gross of fees" inline, states the composition of the policy index, and names the 25% fixed income target so the 27.5% figure is interpretable. A withholds those reference points ("our comparison index," "within our strategic parameters") and buries returns in the fourth paragraph, with one garbled clause about Treasuries and yield spikes. B also fits the tone notes better: it is formatted as a document of record (firm block, date, addressee with title, salutation to the chair and board) and closes by referencing the April 28 meeting, which suits a letter read into the minutes. A reads as a letter to an individual and drifts promotional — "successfully executed a grant distribution," "comfortably," "remains strong," and "pleased to inform you" on a fee change — and uses "our" for the Foundation's payout obligation and assets. B's advantage is substantive clarity and register, not length.
